questions: Dominican patio tranque tie and every detail of the pase de salida
method: five sweeps by source kind (Spanish web, forums and video, apps and code, tournaments, English web), each sweep's decisive claims re-opened by a fact checker, one synthesis, one completeness critic

answers.question: tie
answers.conclusion: The evidence does not support the owner's belief that a tie goes to the blocker as the documented Dominican rule. Only two apps say it: FichaFlow, which labels it its own house rule, and the Phamton140 hobby engine. Neither cites a source. The only Dominican prose source that gives a tie rule next to the blocker-vs-right comparison is DR1 '25, 50, Capicua!'. It gives the tie to the player who placed the first tile of the hand (la mano), and his team takes the points. Its scope is ambiguous: the sentence follows both 'tranquar con el de abajo' and 'tranquar con todo el mundo'. Every Dominican source with a tie rule for the pair-vs-pair tranque also gives the tie to the pair that opened the hand: Wikipedia es regla general (reglamentos-deportes is a copy of it), Domino RD, and La Mesa (patio). Pair-vs-pair variant: the opening pair wins under Dominican regla general. The federation and tournament form (FID, USA federation, Santiago 2019 municipal tournament, 2mino code) scores nothing and redeals. Blocker-wins-ties is Colombian and generic (Kapiku, a Wikipedia regional alternative), not Dominican. The Capi engine already applies the opener rule (packages/engine/src/scoring.ts scoreTrancao: on equal pips, the side that opened the round wins).

answers.question: tie_next_opener
answers.conclusion: Dominican sources agree that the winner of a hand opens the next one: the Wikipedia es Salida bullet, Domino RD, and La Mesa ('la salida no rota'). For a tie, Wikipedia es (Dominican regla general) says the pair that opened the tied hand wins it and opens the next hand. It names the pair, not one player. Phamton140 lets the tie winner (the blocker) open, which follows from its blocker-wins tie rule. The rotating opener (USA federation, FID, dominoarteociencia, Wikipedia's international norm) is federation and generic practice, not Dominican patio. 2mino gives the next hand to the player after the blocker, but only in its nobody-scores variant. Capi's getRoundWinningSeat already has the tie winner open: of the two compared seats, the one on the opening side.

answers.recommendationForCapi: The seat that wins the tie opens the next hand and chooses his tile freely. Under the opening-side tie rule, that is whichever of the two compared seats (the blocker or the next seat) is on the side that opened the tied hand. That seat may not be the player who placed the tied hand's opening tile. This is the current getRoundWinningSeat behavior in reducer.ts, so no change is needed. If the owner switches the tie to the blocker, the blocker opens the next hand.

answers.question: salida_trigger
answers.conclusion: The pase de salida is a real Dominican patio rule, as the owner said. It triggers when the opening tile of a hand is the only tile on the board and the next player (the opponent to the opener's right) cannot play on it and passes. Wikipedia es scopes it to patio (informal) play and gives no equivalent under regla general. A pass later in the hand does not count. It is not universal: the 2025 La Guáyiga municipal tournament rules and the DR1 forum thread do not mention it.

answers.recommendationForCapi: 2v2 only. The trigger is a pass by seat getNextSeat(starterThisRound) while the board holds exactly one tile, the opening tile placed by starterThisRound. That pass makes a pase de salida pending for the opener's team. In reducer state, a pending salida is board.length === 1, passesSinceLastPlay === 1, and the turn on the opener's partner. No new saved field is needed. No other pass in the hand triggers it. Passes are already forced (validate.ts rejects a pass when a legal play exists), so the pass means the player truly cannot play.

answers.question: salida_cancel
answers.conclusion: Yes. Two independent Dominican sources say the salida is cancelled when the opener's partner also cannot play. DR1 says: if the next player after that also has no piece, the points are not counted, and the fourth player plays if he can. Wikipedia es patio says: 'si la pareja tampoco puede jugar entonces se anulan los puntos de salida'. DR1 settles the ambiguous 'la pareja': it means the opener's partner, who plays after the passing opponent. Neither source gives any other cancel condition. Phamton140 cancels only after a double opening and pays 60 when all three pass, but that is one uncited hobby engine. FichaFlow never cancels and calls this its own implementation choice.
supporting: DR1.com, '25, 50, Capicua!' (Wayback, confirmed; 'can be nullified... the points aren't counted'): http://web.archive.org/web/20221014152237/https://dr1.com/articles/dominoes_1.shtml

The turn then goes to the fourth seat as usual. Nothing else cancels it apart from the target cap (see salida_target). Apply the cancel to every opening tile, double or not. Do not copy Phamton140's split by double and non-double.

answers.question: salida_forced_opening
answers.conclusion: A forced opening counts. No source excludes it. Wikipedia es and DR1 define the trigger as the first tile placed, with no exception for the double six that must open the first hand. FichaFlow's worked example is a 6-6 opening that pays the salida. Phamton140 has no exception for the first-hand double six. The evidence is two apps plus the silence of the prose sources, so this is not a stated rule.

answers.recommendationForCapi: Apply the same check whether the opening tile was auto-placed or chosen. The first hand auto-places the highest double: startGame in reducer.ts puts it on the board, and currentTurn is already the next seat. Later hands open with the previous winner's free choice. The check therefore has to work from the initial state of the first hand, where the next seat's first action can already be the triggering pass.

answers.question: salida_every_hand
answers.conclusion: It applies at the start of every hand. DR1 says the play can only occur in the initial play of a hand, when the first domino is thrown down. DR1's earlier phrase 'In an initial game' is best read as the start of a hand, because DR1 uses 'game' to mean a hand elsewhere: its tie sentence calls the player who placed the first domino of the hand 'the player who began the game'. Wikipedia es ties the trigger to the first tile placed, with no first-hand limit. Phamton140 resets the check on every deal. FichaFlow applies it to the first opposing pass after any opening tile.

answers.question: salida_value
answers.conclusion: 25 has the most support. Wikipedia es patio gives '25 o 30 puntos dependiendo de las reglas' and uses the same '25 o 30' for paso corrido and capicúa. It lists targets of 100 or 200, which are Capi's targets, and does not scale the value to the target. DR1 gives 25 for games to 500. The Santiago 2019 tournament uses 25, dominoarteociencia says normally 25, and FichaFlow defaults to 25. The support for 30 is weaker: the Wikipedia alternative, one App Store review (Republica domino), DomiKapikua, and Phamton140 (30 after a double, 60 after a non-double, a split no other source uses). Only DR1 links the value to the target: 10 for games to 200 or 250, 25 for 500. FichaFlow's '10 or 25' repeats DR1 and is not independent.

answers.question: salida_all_pass
answers.conclusion: Under the Dominican prose sources, the opener gets the pase corrido only, not the salida. The partner's pass already cancels the salida (DR1, Wikipedia es). If the fourth player also cannot play, DR1's pase corrido applies: 25 to the last player's team, and he plays again. No source describes the all-pass opening in words. This conclusion combines the two stated rules. The apps disagree. FichaFlow pays the salida at once without cancel and scores paso redondo separately, so it pays both. Phamton140 pays 60 when a double opening makes all three pass, plus a separate pase redondo 30.
supporting: DR1.com, '25, 50, Capicua!' (Wayback, confirmed; the partner's pass cancels, 'the next player plays his piece, if he can'; the pase corrido is 25 and the last player plays again): http://web.archive.org/web/20221014152237/https://dr1.com/articles/dominoes_1.shtml
Wikipedia (es), Dominó dominicano, Puntos de salida (confirmed; partner pass cancels): https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domin%C3%B3
contrary: Phamton140/domino_dominicano scoring_rules.dart determineStartBonus (confirmed; double opening with all three passing pays 60, plus pase redondo 30): https://github.com/Phamton140/domino_dominicano/blob/ba839f33dc6232c854d97d01701a303a8da64a11/lib/engine/rules/scoring_rules.dart

answers.recommendationForCapi: No stacking. The partner's pass cancels the pending salida. The fourth seat's pass then fires the existing pase corrido: +25 to the opener's team if it stays below the target, and the opener plays again. An all-pass opening pays at most 25. The existing VEINTICINCO branch in reducer.ts needs no change.

answers.question: salida_1v1
answers.conclusion: No source addresses the pase de salida in 1v1. Every description is in pair terms: the opener's team, and the cancel by the opener's partner. The Wikipedia es 1v1 (pila) bullet does not mention it. Domino RD's 1v1 has no boneyard and no salida. With Capi's boneyard, the opponent draws until he can play and passes only on an empty boneyard. A pass on the opening tile therefore needs a double opening where the opener holds the rest of that suit and the whole boneyard is drawn. That almost never happens, and there is no partner for the cancel rule.
supporting: Wikipedia (es), Dominó dominicano, Pila bullet (sweep; 1v1 with a pile, no salida mentioned): https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domin%C3%B3
Domino RD (sweep; 1v1 has no draw and no pase de salida): https://dominord.com/rules
DR1.com and Wikipedia es salida text, both in pair terms (confirmed)
answers.recommendationForCapi: 2v2 only, like pase corrido (veinticincoThreshold is Infinity in 1v1). In 1v1 a draw or pass after the opening tile scores nothing. Owner's decision, with no source either way: keep it 2v2-only (recommended), or invent a 1v1 form such as paying when the opponent must draw. No source supports the second option.

answers.question: salida_target
answers.conclusion: No Dominican prose source says whether a salida can reach or pass the target. Two hobby engines disagree. Phamton140 pays salida and pase redondo only while the team is below 170 of 200, and such a bonus can then take the team to 200 and win. 2mino has no salida, but it blocks winning by a pase corrido bonus ('no se puede ganar la partida de pura suerte por un bono'). Capi's existing rule for pase corrido is the same idea as 2mino: a game is won only by winning a round.
supporting: Capi engine pase corrido cap: /Users/Adelson/Desktop/personal/capi/packages/engine/src/reducer.ts (VEINTICINCO branch: pays only if scores[team] + 25 < targetScore)

answers.recommendationForCapi: Use the same cap as pase corrido. At the moment of payment, pay +25 only if scores[openerTeam] + 25 < targetScore. Otherwise drop it: no deferral and no partial payment. A pase de salida never wins the game and never puts a pair at or over the target.

answers.conclusion: The Dominican sources make the salida depend on the partner's action. DR1 says it 'can be nullified', and Wikipedia es says 'se anulan', so the bonus is final only when the opener's partner plays. Neither source says when the scorekeeper writes it down. FichaFlow pays at the pass and never cancels, which its own page calls a deviation from DR1. Phamton140 credits at the pass, but it decides the result by checking the partner's hand in advance, which gives the same outcome as waiting.

answers.recommendationForCapi: The next seat's pass on the one-tile board changes no score and shows no points callout. Pay at the moment the opener's partner places his tile: if board.length === 1 and passesSinceLastPlay === 1 when the partner plays, add +25 to the opener's team, subject to the target check at that moment. Emit a mid-round callout with the payload, like veinticinco. The partner's pass cancels it. Passes are forced, so a look-ahead would give the same result. Paying on the partner's play keeps his hand hidden until he acts, and the state already holds everything needed, so no new saved field is required.

answers.question: other
answers.conclusion: No other opening bonus has support. 'Manito' (Acento.com.do, earlier research) is the name for the opener's partner after the opponent to the opener's right passes, and it carries no points. Neither list has evidence for 'salida matadora' or 'pase de mano'. Other checks agree with Capi. The blocker compares with the player below him ('tranquar con el de abajo') in DR1, Wikipedia es patio, and the 2025 La Guáyiga municipal tournament ('Se tranca con el jugador de abajo'). Pase corrido is 25 in DR1, and the player plays again, with no limit on repeats. La Guáyiga uses 30 for pase corrido and capicúa. FichaFlow says a full block is not a paso redondo, which matches Capi ending the round when the locking tile is placed. The double six opens the first hand, the winner opens later hands, and play goes to the right (Wikipedia es; the DR1 forum says anticlockwise). The Dominican false-pass penalty (pase con ficha, Wikipedia es) cannot happen in Capi, because passes are forced. Phamton140's 30/60 split by double and non-double appears in no other source.

openRisks: The tie decision belongs to the owner. The Capi engine already gives a tranque tie to the side that opened the round (packages/engine/src/scoring.ts scoreTrancao), and the evidence supports that. The owner believes the tie goes to the blocker, and only two apps (FichaFlow as a house rule, Phamton140) support that. The one Dominican prose source for the blocker-vs-right form (DR1) gives the tie to the opener, but its scope is ambiguous. If the owner still wants blocker-wins, it is a one-line change, and it would move away from the better-sourced rule.

The salida value is uncertain. DR1 scales it to 10 for games to 200 or 250, and Capi plays to 100 or 200. At target 100, a flat +25 is a quarter of the target. Wikipedia es (25 or 30, targets 100/200, no scaling) supports 25, but the owner may prefer DR1's 10.

All-pass stacking has no explicit source. The recommendation (the partner's pass cancels the salida, then pase corrido only) combines two stated rules. FichaFlow and Phamton140 both pay two bonuses in that case.

The 1v1 salida and the salida target cap have no Dominican source. Both recommendations follow Capi's existing pase corrido design (2v2 only, a bonus never reaches the target), not documented patio practice.
DR1's live URL is dead (it returns 'conn'). All DR1 evidence comes from Wayback snapshots (2015 and 2022-10-14).

Implementation: the salida adds a new mid-round callout type and payload (types.ts CalloutType), a string in packages/i18n (and the CapiStrings.swift mirror if the Messages extension renders callouts), and a fuzz-invariant update so the scoring-math check includes the new bonus. Per the project rules, real-time behavior needs a four-seat 2v2 test with more than one client.

Saved games in progress when this ships: the recommended check reads only existing fields (board length, passesSinceLastPlay, starterThisRound). An old save paused between the next seat's pass and the partner's play would pay the salida on resume. Confirm that this matches the project's save rules.

Not checked here: the list B paraphrase of DR1 says the tranque winner takes 'the opponent's points'. Capi scores every pip in all hands. That matches Phamton140, but no confirmed Dominican prose source was re-read on this point.

problems.question: tie
problems.problem: The conclusion is stronger than the evidence. (1) The claim that every Dominican source with a pair-vs-pair tie rule gives the tie to the opening pair is false. The Santiago 2019 municipal tournament is Dominican and pair vs pair, and a tie there scores nothing. The synthesis moves it to 'federation and tournament form' only on this question. (2) The Wikipedia 'regla general' tie sentence is called 'Dominican regla general', but the evidence note says the page calls regla general 'más bien la modalidad latina', and the same sentence appears under 'Dominó latino'. dominoarteociencia (generic latino) and pagat's Mexican rule also give the tie to the opener. So opener-wins is generic Latin practice too, and that is the same reason the synthesis uses to dismiss blocker-wins as 'Colombian and generic, not Dominican'. (3) Capi does not use pair totals. For Capi's exact comparison (the blocker against the next seat), the direct evidence is DR1 on one side, and its scope is ambiguous: the 2015-snapshot evidence item places the tie sentence under 'tranquar con todo el mundo', not 'con el de abajo'. On the other side are FichaFlow and Phamton140, both uncited. No source settles it. (4) The synthesis lists Capi's own scoreTrancao as supporting evidence. That is circular. openRisks says 'the evidence supports that' and calls the change a move 'away from the better-sourced rule', and both statements overstate the evidence.
problems.fix: Restate the conclusion like this: no Dominican source states the tie rule for the blocker-vs-right comparison. Opener-wins is the nearest documented rule, by analogy from DR1's other variant and from regla general, which is Latin. Blocker-wins is the convention in two Dominican-labeled apps. Remove scoreTrancao from the supporting list. Give the owner a real A/B choice and say that no source contradicts his belief for the exact rule Capi uses. Keep the confidence at low.

problems.question: tie_next_opener
problems.problem: The recommendation conflicts with the source that Capi's tie rule rests on. DR1 says the player who placed the first tile 'is by default the winner'. It names a player, not a side. Dominican sources agree that the winner opens the next hand, so under DR1 the original opener opens after a tie. getRoundWinningSeat (reducer.ts lines 443-450) picks the compared seat on the opening side instead. That seat differs from the opener whenever the opener's partner is one of the two compared seats: blocker S with rival W, or blocker E with rival S, when N opened. That is half of the 2v2 tie cases. Wikipedia names only the pair. So 'no change needed' is a Capi choice, not the sourced rule, and a confidence of medium is too high for it.
problems.fix: Mark this as the owner's decision. If he follows DR1, getRoundWinningSeat returns state.starterThisRound when payload.blockerPips === payload.rivalPips (the payload already carries both). In that case, also change the rules copy 'Después de un tranque, sale el que ganó el tranque: el que trancó o el jugador a su derecha.' and its English line in packages/i18n/src/rules.ts.

problems.question: salida_timing
problems.problem: The payment predicate is ambiguous for 1v1. The recommendation says 'if board.length === 1 and passesSinceLastPlay === 1 when the partner plays'. The same state occurs in 1v1: the opponent passes on an empty boneyard, and the turn goes back to the opener, who then plays. If the check reads only the two fields, as the salida_trigger text suggests ('No new saved field is needed'), it pays a 1v1 salida to the opener. That contradicts the salida_1v1 recommendation.
problems.fix: State the full guard: state.is2v2 && seat === getNextSeat(getNextSeat(state.starterThisRound, true), true) && state.board.length === 1 && state.passesSinceLastPlay === 1, followed by the target check. Add a 1v1 unit test with exactly that state and assert that no bonus is paid.

problems.question: salida_timing
problems.problem: Paying on the partner's play conflicts with code the synthesis does not name. (1) invariants.fuzz.test.ts line 192 asserts 'no score change mid-round play', and this design makes that assertion fail by intent. (2) Both clients hard-code the mid-round banner to veinticinco: apps/web/src/app/game/[id]/page.tsx line 888 and apps/mobile/app/game/[id].tsx line 1187. A new 'salida' callout during play would render as the full-screen round-end CalloutOverlay unless both checks change. (3) The engine runs only on the server (apps/web move route), so the rule goes live for every client at the web deploy. App Store builds that are already installed look up CALLOUT_CONFIG, get nothing, and render no overlay. They still play the callout sound, because playCallout fires on any lastCallout, and the score jumps by 25 with no explanation. openRisks mentions only a new callout type, a string, and a generic fuzz update.
problems.fix: Add these items to the implementation plan. Change line 192 to allow exactly +25 to the opener's team under the salida guard. Add 'salida' to both isMidRoundCallout checks and to both CALLOUT_CONFIG maps. Decide the rollout order: either ship the engine change after the mobile build with the banner is live, or accept the unexplained +25 on old builds. Following observation #29, add reach-tally entries (salida paid, cancelled by the partner's pass, capped at the target, cancel followed by pase corrido) and run one mutation per rule.

problems.question: salida_trigger / salida_value
problems.problem: The synthesis uses a non-Dominican source as Dominican and classifies sources differently on different questions. dominoarteociencia is generic 'dominó latino' in the earlier research, and the tie_next_opener answer labels it 'generic'. salida_trigger and salida_value still cite it as support, with no label ('normally 25'). The Santiago 2019 tournament supports the patio salida here but is dismissed as 'tournament form' for the tie. The synthesis also omits La Guáyiga 2025 (Dominican, unverified) from salida_value, although it uses 30 for pase corrido and capicúa, which supports 'Wikipedia: 25 or 30' and the case for 30.
problems.fix: Use one classification for each source on every question. For 25, the Dominican support is Wikipedia patio ('25 o 30'), the Santiago 2019 tournament (25, target unknown), and the FichaFlow default. Label dominoarteociencia as generic. Add La Guáyiga to the evidence for 30. The recommendation of +25 can stay, with confidence medium.

problems.question: salida_value
problems.problem: The synthesis summarizes DR1 as '10 for games to 200 or less'. DR1 names only 200, 250 and 500. It says nothing about games to 100, which is Capi's default target. Applying DR1's scaling at target 100 is an extrapolation.
problems.fix: Write 'DR1: 10 for games to 200 or 250, 25 for 500, no value given for 100'. In the owner's decision, say that the DR1 option at target 100 has no source.

problems.question: salida_timing / edge cases
problems.problem: The synthesis does not cover a round that ends before the partner plays. In 2v2 nothing can come between the trigger and the payment. The partner acts next. His play cannot be a dominó, because he holds 7 tiles. It cannot be a tranque, because two tiles on the board cannot use up a suit. validate.ts rejects draws in 2v2. The only other exit is a claim (forfeit.ts, 2 minutes of silence, live mode only), and a claim ends the game, so the unpaid salida does not matter. Without this statement, an implementer can add a deferral or cleanup path that is never needed. The synthesis also does not cover turn-based 2v2 games from iMessage. In those games the partner's play can come hours after the pass, and the design shows no pending state.
problems.fix: Add a sentence: in 2v2 the payment decision always happens at the partner's next action, and a round cannot end first, so no pending state or cleanup is needed. Add an owner decision: show a 'pase de salida pendiente' notice at the pass (with no points), or show nothing until the partner plays.

problems.question: salida_forced_opening
problems.problem: The code pointer is wrong. reducer.ts has no startGame function. The auto-placement is in createInitialState (reducer.ts lines 134-184), which sets board to [starterTile], currentTurn to the next seat, passesSinceLastPlay to 0, and lastPlayedBy to the starter. The synthesis also leaves out a fact it could state: in 2v2 all 28 tiles are dealt, so the first hand always opens with the 6-6. The trigger then fires when the next seat holds no six, which is about 5.5% of first hands (C(15,7)/C(21,7)).
problems.fix: Replace 'startGame' with createInitialState. Say that the predicate already holds in the initial state, and add a unit test that starts from createInitialState with a seeded deal where the next seat holds no six.

problems.question: tie / other (implementation scope)
problems.problem: The synthesis understates the work. It says a tie switch is 'one line in scoreTrancao, plus a test'. The fuzz suite also encodes the opener tie (expectedTranque, the comment on line 84, the assertion on line 222), and the rules copy states it in both languages: 'Si empatan, gana el lado que salió en esa ronda.' and 'A tie goes to the side that opened the round.' For the salida, openRisks lists only a callout string. packages/i18n/src/rules.ts needs a new rules section (2v2 only, +25, the partner's pass cancels it, it never wins the game, next to 'Un pase corrido nunca da la partida'), and What's New needs an update. The CapiStrings.swift item is conditional in openRisks, but the answer is known: the Messages extension renders callouts through GameWebView (the web page), so no Swift change is needed.
problems.fix: List the fuzz expectation, both rules.ts language blocks, and What's New for each change. Remove the Swift mirror item.

problems.question: salida_every_hand
problems.problem: The confidence 'high' is stronger than the evidence. DR1's own paragraph opens with 'In an initial game'. Wikipedia's 'al momento de colocarse la primera ficha' does not say whether it means the first tile of the hand or of the game. The other support comes from two apps.
problems.fix: Lower the confidence to medium. The recommendation (every hand, at most once, only with one tile on the board) can stay.

problems.question: salida_target
problems.problem: The recommendation has no source, but it is presented as settled, while the 1v1 answer, which is in the same position, is marked as an owner decision. The synthesis also lists Phamton140's rule under contrary, although that rule partly agrees: it stops the bonuses near the target (at 170 of 200). It differs only because a bonus paid from below 170 can still win the game.
problems.fix: Mark it as an owner decision that follows Capi's existing pase corrido rule. Describe Phamton140 as a different cap, not as the opposite rule.

problems.question: openRisks (tranque points)
problems.problem: A question that affects every tranque is still open. Does the winner take every pip in all hands (Capi now) or only the opponents' pips (the DR1 paraphrase in list B)? This question affects more rounds than the salida does. The support for 'all hands' is Phamton140 and Rafael Bras, who writes about Puerto Rican play. Neither is a Dominican prose source.
problems.fix: Re-read the tranque paragraph in the DR1 Wayback snapshot before shipping. If it says 'the opponent's points', give the question to the owner. The current rules copy promises all pips.

critic.verdict: You can act on the pase de salida part once the guards and integration notes above are added. The trigger, the partner's-pass cancel, every hand, +25, 2v2 only, the target cap, and no stacking on an all-pass opening all match the confirmed Dominican evidence or Capi's existing design. I checked the no-new-field claim: passesSinceLastPlay and starterThisRound have no writers outside the engine. Two things need fixing before implementation. First, the payment predicate needs explicit is2v2 and partner-seat guards, or it pays a salida in 1v1. Second, the plan must list the conflicting fuzz invariant (line 192), the veinticinco-only mid-round banner checks in both clients, and the rollout to old App Store builds. Do not show the tranque tie section to the owner as it stands. For the blocker-vs-right comparison that Capi uses, no source settles the tie. Opener-wins rests on analogy from a Latin regla general and from an ambiguous DR1 sentence. Blocker-wins rests on two uncited Dominican apps. The owner's belief is therefore not contradicted, and the choice is his. The next-opener-after-tie behavior also differs from DR1, which names the opening player. Two findings would change this verdict. A Dominican prose source that states the tie rule for 'tranquar con el de abajo' would settle the tie. A source that pays the salida at the pass with no partner cancel would reopen the timing and cancel answers. Observation logged: #33, 'A research synthesis must classify each source the same way on every question and keep analogy apart from direct evidence'.

sweeps.notes:
MAIN FINDING. No new source gives a tie rule for the Dominican patio tranque, where the blocker compares with the next player. The Spanish Wikipedia 'Dominó' article (read as raw wikitext, so the quotes are exact) says two things in its Dominican section. Under 'regla general', a tied tranque goes to the pair that opened ('la pareja que salió'), and that pair also opens the next hand. For patio, it says only that the blocker compares his own tiles with the opponent on his right. It gives no separate patio tie rule. Whether the 'pair that opened' tie rule carries over to patio is an open reading; the source does not state it. So the only source that says 'a tie goes to the blocker' for the Dominican blocker-vs-next rule is still FichaFlow (confirmed on its second page, /learn/guide). The closest analog found is Colombian 'el que cierra responde': the closer must have fewer points than the opponents, and a tie goes to the closing team. That supports the user's recollection by analogy only. Other individual-comparison variants give the tie to the opener (Maracaibo, eastern Cuba) or score nothing (Puerto Rican ponceño). The generic Wikipedia rule lists 'opener' and 'blocker' as regional alternatives to the international norm (a draw, and the next player after the opener opens).

PASE DE SALIDA. The Wikipedia Dominican section confirms the trigger (the immediate opponent cannot play on the first tile), the value (25 or 30 'dependiendo de las reglas'), and the cancel rule (the partner also cannot play). It says only 'la primera ficha'. It does not say whether this means every hand or only the first hand of the game, and it does not mention forced openings, 1v1, the target score, or the all-three-pass case. The same section says only the first hand is opened by the double-six holder. Later hands are opened by the previous hand's winner, so later openings are chosen, not forced. FichaFlow's guide says 'Dominican variants use 10 or 25' (this matches DR1). FichaFlow also says it awards the 25 at once and does not cancel it; this is an app implementation note. No source answered salida_forced_opening, salida_every_hand, salida_all_pass, salida_1v1, or salida_target explicitly.

verified.question: salida_all_pass
verified.rule: If the opening tile is a double and none of the three other players can play, the opener's team gets the full 60-point salida; pase redondo (+30) is a separate check run after three consecutive passes.

verified.note: scoring_rules.dart lines 56-57 have the comment and 'return StartBonusType.double60;' on separate lines. The team gets 60 (bonusSalidaCompletaDoble). Otherwise the round ends in a tranque. Caveat: Round holds one _pendingImmediateBonus slot. The salida 60 is set on the first pass and the pase redondo 30 on the third pass. The two bonuses stack only if the caller runs Game.applyPendingBonuses after each pass, as its doc comment requires ('Debe llamarse después de cada pase que pueda generar una bonificación'). If the caller skips that call, the +30 overwrites the 60.

verified.question: salida_timing
verified.rule: The salida and pase redondo bonuses are credited at the moment of the pass, not at the end of the round; the partner cancel is decided at that moment by a look-ahead check of whether the partner and fourth player hold a playable tile.
verified.quote: Los pases de salida y los pases redondos otorgan puntos en el momento en que ocurren, no al finalizar la ronda.
verified.note: The exact sentence is in the ImmediateBonus doc comment, round.dart lines 12-13, split across two '///' lines. Look-ahead: _evaluateStartPassBonus (lines 332-333) calls canPlay(partnerIndex) and canPlay(afterPartnerIndex) when the next player passes. These calls test the hands of the partner and the fourth player against the board with only the opening tile, before those players take their turns. Precision: Round only stores _pendingImmediateBonus. The points reach the team score in Game.applyPendingBonuses, which the caller must run after each pass.

verified.question: salida_target
verified.rule: Salida and pase redondo bonuses apply only while the team has fewer than 170 points (target 200); after a bonus is added the engine runs its game-end check, so a bonus from below 170 can take a team to 200 and end the game.
verified.quote: // Regla de los 170: solo se aplican bonos de salida/pase redondo // si el equipo tiene menos de 170 puntos.
verified.note: The quote is on game.dart lines 145-146 as two comment lines. The gate is ScoringRules.canReceivePassBonus(team.score), which is 'teamScore < ScoringConstants.threshold170' (170). It checks the score before the bonus is added. isPassBonus is a string match on reason containing 'Pase' or 'pase', and all three bonus reasons match ('Pase de salida con doble', 'Pase de salida con ficha normal', 'Pase redondo'). A gated bonus is cleared, not deferred. Otherwise team.addPoints(bonus.points) runs, then _checkGameEnd(). _checkGameEnd uses Team.reached200, which is 'score >= 200' in models/team.dart, and it does not cap the score. So a team at 140-169 that gets a 60 salida reaches 200 or more and wins, for example 169 + 60 = 229.

sweeps.notes: Main new finding: the DR1 article '25, 50, Capicua!' (dr1.com/articles/dominoes_1.shtml) is the same one earlier research cited for pase de salida. It also has a tie rule: a tied tranque goes to the player who placed the first tile (la mano), and his team scores. This contradicts FichaFlow's 'a tie favors the blocker', even though FichaFlow cites DR1 as a source. It agrees with Spanish Wikipedia 'Dominó' (Regla General pair totals: the pair that opened wins the tie and opens the next hand). Spanish Wikipedia gives no tie rule for the patio blocker-vs-right comparison. The DR1 tie sentence comes right after the 'tranquar con todo el mundo' sentence, so it is ambiguous whether it also covers 'con el de abajo'. The DR1 salida paragraph starts 'In an initial game' but later says the bonus happens on 'the initial play of a hand'. That leaves every-hand versus first-hand-only ambiguous. The live dr1.com returns only the word 'conn' to WebFetch and curl. I read it through a Wayback snapshot (20221014152237) with curl; WebFetch cannot reach web.archive.org. Dead ends: dominord.com/rules ('Domino RD' app) is behind a Cloudflare challenge (403). The La Guáyiga 2025 Dominican municipal tournament lists no pase de salida bonus at all. It uses 30 for paso corrido and capicúa, and 'Se tranca con el jugador de abajo'.
